notes.title: QOL Patch v0.8.5g
notes.content:
Patch v0.8.5g

Howdy everyone, 

Over the last couple days I've been looking into why Metropolis 1998 utilizes my CPU at 100% despite the game using only a fraction of a frame in the CPU profiler. 

Turns out it's: [olist]
[*] An NVIDIA graphics driver bug when Thread Optimization is active (which it is by default) and the game is windowed (not full screen).
[*] An NVIDIA graphics driver bug when the game is running full screen (whether or not Thread Optimization is active)
[/olist]
Note that VSYNC is active in both scenarios

Thread optimization is good for larger, 3D games; but it causes issues for smaller games and older version of OpenGL (double whammy for Metropolis 1998)

What's happening behind the scenes is that when there's leftover time before the next frame can begin executing, the CPU (thread) is instructed to wait. There's two types of waiting: sleep and busy-wait. The trade off between the two is: [olist]
[*] Sleep wait does not utilize the CPU thread. The fan stay silent. However, it is slower to grab/reactivate.
[*] Busy wait utilizes 100% of the CPU thread. The fans stay on full power. It's faster to reactivate.
[/olist]
I managed to figure out a way around both issues. 

[b]For window mode:[/b] I downloaded the NVIDIA SDK and now Metropolis 1998 will automatically create a NVIDIA profile that explicitly disables Thread Optimization just for my game. If you don't have an NVIDIA GPU, nothing will happen. 

[b]For full screen mode:[/b] Since Threaded Optimization on or off made no difference, instead what I'm doing is calculating how much time there is before the next frame can fire off and explicitly calling sleep() on the active CPU thread, right before everything is drawn to the screen. I subtract 2 milliseconds from sleep period so there's some buffer. I tried subtracting just 1 millisecond but that causes occasional and barely perceptible issues. 

[Just be sure to reset the timer after display() is called, and dont call sleep() if the frame falls below refreshRate - buffer]

My CPU fans being at full power annoyed the heck out of me, and Im so glad I figured out a way to play my game in peace.


Also, it looks like I accidentally uploaded an experimental feature where the outdoor lighting and breeze animations are set to 12 FPS. Oops! I'll fix it in the next patch.

notes.title: Demo Updated! Lots of new features
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

After 5 months of work I have finally released a major update to the demo! Things are starting to come together into a real game, though this build is still pre-alpha :)

See below for all the updates!

Metropolis 1998 - Release Notes

[b]Major Changes[/b]
 [list]
[*]  Load on Demand implemented for more efficient GPU processing
[*]   Commercial, Service, and Municple demand implemented (stage one, basic)
[*]   Residential demand implemented. NOTE: Right now it's random, but the value effects the rate people will move in. Random is temporary.
[*]   Unit animations, sitting/sleeping, and color variants
[*]   Vehicle color variants
[*]   Basic terrain modification (no height or water yet)
[*]   Much more efficient saving/loading times and reduced save file size
[*]   More unit activities (like going out to lunch while at work)
[*]   Families added (basic implementation). Will move in together.
[*]   You can place auto grow zones and buildings have construction animations. NOTE: Right now you can only place for low density, and there's only one allowed depth. This will be expanded in future builds.
[*]   Map / terrain is now procedurally generated
[*]   Potato graphics mode. All windows become opaque, and only the visible top floors all outdoor items are drawn by the GPU
[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
 [list]
[*]  Units can now path across a road when entering/exiting a driveway
[*]   Units are assigned clothing + color based on their job (most businesses do not have this feature yet)
[*]   Roof texture will output on all floors now (instead of flat roof below top floor)
[*]   GUI Updated. Also added current weather icon
[*]   Wind is no longer constant
[*]   Buildings can no longer be edited when connected to road. NOTE: This will soon become a button the player can press to add the building to the market. 
[*]   New assets
[*]   Unit wont claim a parking spot until it enters the buildings property
[*]   Blueprints can now be mirrored (press T)
[*]   Units can now properly path in 3D space (where as before they could only use one staircase)
[*]   Outdoor objects are no longer deleted when an outdoor floor is placed (excluding driveways)
[*]   Press B to open delete menu

notes.title: April 2024 - Development Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

There will not be an update pushed out this month. After PAX East, I had to focus on some IRL things outside of work for a few weeks. Since then, I've been hard at work on adding and improving features to the game. I hope to release the next update by the end of May, but there's no set date yet. This update will be much bigger than previous updates, though half of the work is "invisible". 

The big invisible changes involve improving the core game engine. I've added LOD (load on demand) which was a lot of work, but was necessary to build larger cities. Previously, every asset in the game was being sent to the GPU, which was causing the FPS to tank once a lot of assets were outputted to the world, even if they were off screen. I also spent some time significantly improving the save/load time and file size--After the changes I made, there's been a 75%-90% improvement. There's also a handful of smaller adjustments that were causing the game to tank CPU performance. Lastly, a good amount of work went into creating color variants via the GPU (instead of creating every single sprite by hand)


Some of the visible changes that are now implemented are:
[list]
[*] Basic terrain output (no terrain height though)
[*] Unit animations, sitting positions, and color variants
[*] More unit activities (liking going out to eat)
[*] Auto grow residential zones (just like the classic city builder experience
[/list]

Upcoming major additions include:
[list]
[*] RICO demand (this will be fleshed out over months)
[*] Water (terrain and pools)
[*] Possibly terrain height (but cant build on it yet)
[*] More unit activities like shopping, relaxing, chores
[*] Construction animations
[*] Possibly unit families, education, friends, etc.
[*] Hopefully street parking
[*] Possibly color variants for every item in game
[/list]

There's also a big list of minor improvements/bug fixes, but I'll share those as part of update-release announcement.

- Chase

notes.title: What to expect while pre-alpha
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

I'm getting closer to releasing the next update/build of the game. With that around the corner, I'd like to clarify what pre-alpha means for Metropolis 1998. 

The game is undergoing rapid evolution (new features, changes to current features). Adding new features and fixing bugs is my main focus while pre-alpha. This essentially means that when I upload the build to steam, it will be a full replacement of all files from the previous build [b](including save files and user-made blueprints!)[/b]. Unfortunately as a self-funded, micro indie studio (I'm the sole developer), I do not have the bandwidth to facilitate a smooth transition between each build during this phase of development. 

That being said, after the next update, I'm going to see if it's possible to not lose user-created blueprints, cause that hurts the most. 

I am not sure if it's possible to opt out of auto-updates from Steam. If you dont want to lose your save files/blueprints, you can download the game from itch.io (from the website) which will not auto-update when I release a new build (you'd have to re-download the game to get the update).

What to expect in the next build?
- Parking lots in zones
- Ability to subdivide buildings (for now, you can create separate living spaces (e.g. apartments) in residential zones)
- Ability to click on buildings, units, and cars to see basic info
- Improved GPU performance (note: I have put 0 effort into efficient GPU code! This will just be the first step in a long series of planned improvements)
- Bug fixes

Full list of changes will be given with the update announcement.

Since March, the user interface is being redeveloped from scratch based on user feedback. I took a lot of inspiration from Rollercoaster Tycoon and OpenRCT 2.
